Sandboxed microVMs for AI coding agents.

Usage: agent-vm [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  setup      Acquire and verify the boot image (run once first)
  msb        Forward arguments to the bundled `msb` with agent-vm's MSB_HOME/MSB_PATH pinned (e.g.
             `agent-vm msb ls`, `agent-vm msb status`). Relies on `needs_msb_setup` staying true for
             this variant — see main()
  clipboard  Exchange a string between the host and the sandbox
  doctor     Diagnostic / maintenance operations for agent-vm's private microsandbox state (e.g.
             --reset-msb-db)
  secret     Manage agent-vm's own values in the host system keychain
  image      Inspect the selected boot image, acquire it into the image cache, explicitly retain a
             default, or build/import a finished image. Only `show` is offline; only build/import
             may invoke Docker
  shell      Launch shell in a per-project sandbox; tool arguments are forwarded verbatim
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version  Print version

Sandbox resources:
      --memory <GIB>  Sandbox memory, in GiB [env: AGENT_VM_MEMORY_GIB] [default: 2]
      --cpus <N>      vCPU count for the sandbox [env: AGENT_VM_CPUS] [default: 2]

GitHub access:
      --no-git             Don't inject host gh/git credentials into the guest
      --repo <OWNER/REPO>  Add a repo to the GitHub allow-list (repeatable)

Credentials:
      --allow-missing-credentials  Launch even when a requested YAML credential is missing or
                                   unreadable

Mounts & ports:
      --mount <HOST[:GUEST][:MODE]...>
          Bind an extra host path into the guest, or seed a persistent fork (repeatable)
  -p, --publish <[BIND:]HOST_PORT:GUEST_PORT>
          Publish a guest TCP port to the host, docker-style (repeatable)
      --auto-publish
          Auto-forward every guest listener onto the host (Lima-style)

Network egress:
      --allow-egress <[tcp://|udp://]IP|CIDR[:PORT] | [tcp://]HOST[:PORT]>
          Allow one IP/CIDR or TLS hostname, optionally transport/port-scoped (repeatable)
      --allow-internet-egress[=<BOOL>]
          Allow public internet egress and DNS. Guest egress is denied by default [possible values:
          true, false]
      --allow-lan[=<BOOL>]
          Allow Private RFC1918, 100.64/10 and fc00::/7. Does not itself grant internet or DNS
          [possible values: true, false]
      --allow-host[=<BOOL>]
          Allow host loopback services through host.microsandbox.internal, including the host DNS
          resolver. Does not itself grant internet [possible values: true, false]

Image:
      --image <REF>   Boot this image instead of the configured one [env: AGENT_VM_IMAGE_TAG]
      --update-check  Check the registry for a newer image at launch (opt-in)

Guest user:
      --root  Run the guest as root (uid 0) instead of the default host user

Getting started:
  agent-vm setup       fetch and verify the boot image (run once first)
  cd ~/your-project
  agent-vm <tool>      launch one of the tools listed above

Launch options go before the tool: agent-vm [launch options] <tool> [tool arguments...]
Every argument after the tool is forwarded to it verbatim, including --help and --.
Built-in commands take their own options after the command and no launch options.
`agent-vm help <tool>` shows examples; `agent-vm doctor` shows which config files were
found and what they resolved to.
